evidence: Cic. Att. 9.14.2: nūllum diem (sc. praetermittere; Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A description: Traupman’s word for a call with the participle of praetermittere, to let a day or a chance go by. No reference work has a word for a missed call. In talk Latin says it with a verb: “he called and you didn’t answer” (see the examples).

phrases.latin: Avus tē bis compellāvit, nec respondistī.
phrases.english: Grandpa called you twice, and you didn’t answer.

phrases.latin: Tēlephōnēma tuum praetermīsī: in balneō eram.
phrases.english: I missed your call: I was in the bath.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 391.
